sentences.text:
Petitioners have filed the present petition and have sought for issuance of appropriate writ to declare that the acquisition proceedings, initiated vide Preliminary Notification dated 06.04.1989 issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short 'the Act') by the 2 nd respondent and the final notification dated 25.03.1991 issued under Section 6(1) of the Act by the 1st respondent, has lapsed.
2.
Sri. C. M. Nagabushana, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the lands of the petitioners were notified as per preliminary notification issued on 06.04.1989.
It is further submitted that on 25.03.1991, final notification has been issued.
It is submitted that till date, no award has been passed as regards the petitioners' properties despite lapse of 32 years.
3. It is noticed however that the writ petition filed by 1st petitioner in W.P.No.28439/1991 assailing the land NC: 2023:KHC:21050 acquisition notification was allowed on 19.06.1998.
However, the said order was set aside by the Division Bench in W.A.No. 1490/1999 on 01.08.2001.
Ever since the said date, it is submitted that no action has been taken to pass award and complete the acquisition proceedings in terms of the statutory scheme.
4. Reliance is placed on the order passed in W.A.No.3469/2012 as regards the same notifications.

The observations made therein at Paragraph Nos.3 and 4 are self-explanatory, which read as follows:
"Learned counsel for the parties admit that, W.A.No.3464/2012, which was also filed against the same order of the learned Single Judge, has been dismissed by a Division Bench of this Court vide Judgment and Order dated 12.06.2015.

It has further been accepted by learned counsel for the parties that the Special Leave to Appeal No.28602/2015 filed against the said Judgment passed in Writ Appeal No.3464/2012 has also been dismissed by the Apex Court by a NC: 2023:KHC:21050 speaking order dated 02.11.2015, the operative portion of which is reproduced below:

"For the reasons stated above, without going into the merits of the case, I.A.1/14 filed by the second respondent has to be allowed, holding acquisition proceedings initiated by the appellants and the State Government under Secs.4(1) and 6(1) of the L.A. Act,
1894, for acquiring the land belonging to the second respondent, shall be deemed to have lapsed by friction (sic) of Sec.24(2) of the Act, 2013 and the writ appeal filed by the appellant-Board does not survive for consideration and it is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, I.A.1/2014 filed by the second respondent under Sec. 151 of CPC is allowed and writ appeal is dismissed holding that it does not survive for consideration."
4. In view of the dismissal of the W.A.No.3464/2012 and for the reasons given in the Judgment of the said writ appeal as well as the order passed by the Apex Court in Special Leave NC:
2023:KHC:21050 to Appeal No.28602/2015, these writ appeals are also dismissed.

5. Such of the facts relating to the order in W.A.No.3469/2012 and the order passed in S.L.P.(C)No.
28602/2015 have not been controverted.

6. Sri. V. Karthik, learned counsel appearing for respondents 2 and 3 submits that insofar as the orders passed as referred above including dismissal of S.L.P.(C)No. 28602/2015, the same are not in dispute.
7. Perused paragraph No.8 of the statement of objections filed by respondents 2 and 3.

The same reads as follows:
"The further averments in Para 6 & 7 about further challenge on the ground of no sanction to the scheme in WP No.9593/2007, which was accepted by the learned Single Judge and in WA No.3469/2012 and other connected matters on account of repealing of Land Acquisition Act and coming into force of Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & NC:
2023:KHC:21050 Resettlement Act, 2013, Writ Appeal came to be disposed of holding that acquisition proceedings has been lapsed and dismissal of SL P No.28602/2015 are not in dispute"
8.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & NC
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Accordingly, in the present matter also taking note that no action has been taken within a reasonable period of time to complete the acquisition proceedings and taking note of the order passed in W.A.No.3469/2012, petitioners are entitled for declaration that the acquisition proceedings as per preliminary and final notification passed by respondents at Annexures-B and C,
insofar as petitioners' lands are concerned has lapsed.
9.
Accordingly, petition is disposed off.
I.A.1/2023 filed for early disposal is allowed.
